answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 1% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the mirror fee is applied at the vine exit, the yarrow audit totals the burn and the ledger publishes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 20 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
